## Incident Report — 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (confirmed via mDNS self-registration and Kerberos `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` machine account) |
| AD domain | spoonwatch.net (DC: SPOONWATCH-DC, 192.168.1.2) |
| Logged-in user | steve.smith (Kerberos `CNameString`, frames to/from 192.168.1.2) |

### Malware family
**Vidar Stealer** (also tracked as a Vidar-family info-stealer). **Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no Suricata/IDS alert files were present in the evidence set, so this call is based entirely on TTP fingerprinting in the pcap:

1. At t=203s the host makes a raw TCP connection straight to an IP literal (`2.56.57.108:80`), with no preceding DNS lookup — classic hardcoded-C2 stealer behavior.
2. It POSTs 25-byte check-in beacons to `/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` and receives back seven Windows PE32 DLLs mislabeled as `image/jpeg`. `strings` on the recovered DLLs shows the exact dependency set Vidar pulls down to read/decrypt browser data stores: `sqlite3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `nssckbi.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, plus VC++ runtime DLLs.
3. It then POSTs an empty check-in to `/osk//main.php`.
4. It finally POSTs a 379,629-byte multipart body (`Content-Type: zip`, filename `_5861695120.zip`) to `/osk/`. Carving and unzipping that body yields a stolen-data archive with folders `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, plus `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `system.txt`, and `screenshot.jpg` — the exact log layout Vidar produces on each infected machine.

This download-modules-then-upload-zip-of-stolen-data cycle, the request headers (`Accept-Language: ru-RU`, no `User-Agent`), and the Apache/Win32/PHP 5.3 C2 backend are all consistent with known Vidar deployments, but nothing in the traffic contains an explicit self-identifying string, so I'm calling this behavioral rather than signature-confirmed.

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` — plaintext HTTP, contacted directly by IP with no DNS resolution observed anywhere in the capture (evidence: `tcp.stream 65`, frames 1498–12328+).

**Domain**
- None observed. The C2 was never resolved via DNS in this capture — access was hardcoded to the IP literal above.

**URLs (all POST, host `2.56.57.108`, stream 65)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (exfiltration POST, `Content-Length: 379629`, `Content-Type: zip`)

**Transferred files / SHA256 (module downloads, all served as `Content-Type: image/jpeg` but are PE32 DLLs)**
| Downloaded as | Actual type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 1.jpg | PE32 DLL (console), bundles `sqlite3.dll` | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| 2.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| 3.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| 4.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| 5.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI), bundles `mozglue.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `nssckbi.dll`, `softokn3.dll` | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| 6.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| 7.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |

**Exfiltrated file**
- Filename (from `Content-Disposition`): `_5861695120.zip`
- SHA256 of the raw ZIP payload (carved from the `POST /osk/` body, `PK\x03\x04` to `PK\x05\x06`): `5d4be98187cae207e49d4c326d00510e461f054d0f7c28066468100534483851`
- Archive contents confirm data theft: `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/*`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`.

### Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user steve.smith on the spoonwatch.net AD domain, was infected with a Vidar-family information stealer. The malware pulled seven auxiliary DLLs disguised as `.jpg` files from `2.56.57.108:80/osk/` to gain SQLite and NSS browser-decryption capability, then harvested Chrome/Edge autofill data, cookies, saved passwords, Outlook data, system info, and a desktop screenshot, packaged it into `_5861695120.zip`, and exfiltrated it back to the same IP over plaintext HTTP. The initial infection vector is not present in this capture — traffic begins at host boot/DHCP and the stealer is already resident and beaconing within the first 3.5 minutes.
